gig.title: Advanced Browser Automation & Website Reverse Engineering Developer
gig.description: **Long-Term Opportunity | Bangla Communication Mandatory** I'm looking for a highly skilled, experienced, and independent **Browser Automation & Website Reverse Engineering Specialist** for a long-term project. I need someone who can deeply analyze how websites work, understand browser behavior, investigate complex technical issues, identify root causes, and develop reliable solutions. **My priority is simple: I need working solutions, not just code.** ## Required Technical Expertise - Advanced JavaScript and/or Python programming - Tampermonkey Userscripts and Chrome Extensions - Browser Automation (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, etc.) - Advanced DOM manipulation and MutationObserver - Dynamic websites, SPAs, and asynchronous JavaScript - AJAX, Fetch API, REST APIs, JSON, and WebSockets - HTTP/HTTPS requests, headers, cookies, sessions, and authentication flows - Browser DevTools and advanced network debugging - JavaScript debugging, execution flow analysis, and reverse engineering - Browser events, page lifecycle, and navigation behavior - API request/response analysis - Error detection, root-cause analysis, and troubleshooting - Performance optimization and reliable automation architecture ## Core Responsibilities **1. Complete Website Behavior Analysis** Analyze the website's functionality, frontend architecture, JavaScript behavior, DOM structure, navigation flow, browser events, and dynamic interactions. **2. Advanced Network & API Investigation** Investigate network requests, API endpoints, request/response structures, session behavior, and communication between the frontend and backend. **3. Browser Behavior & Execution Analysis** Understand how the browser processes website actions, executes JavaScript, handles asynchronous operations, manages application state, and responds to user interactions. **4. Independent Problem Investigation** Identify the actual cause of technical problems without depending entirely on step-by-step instructions. **5. End-to-End Problem Solving** Design, implement, test, and optimize complete technical solutions rather than providing partial fixes or temporary workarounds. **6. Long-Term Maintenance** Maintain and update automation solutions as websites change, resolve compatibility issues, and continuously improve stability and performance. ## Complete Technical Freedom You are free to select the most suitable technologies, programming languages, frameworks, and technical approaches. You are not limited to Tampermonkey. You may use JavaScript, Python, Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, browser extensions, backend services, APIs, or other appropriate tools. **I care about the final result, reliability, and effectiveness — not which specific tool or method you use.** All technical approaches must be secure, authorized, and appropriate for the project. ## What I Expect I need a developer who: - Thinks independently and approaches problems analytically - Understands how modern websites and browsers actually work - Can investigate complex issues using browser and network debugging tools - Can identify root causes instead of repeatedly applying temporary fixes - Can develop complete, reliable, and maintainable solutions - Can adapt when websites change their structure or behavior - Takes responsibility for testing and verifying their solutions - Communicates clearly and provides meaningful technical explanations **I do not want someone who simply follows instructions or writes basic scripts. I need a technically capable problem-solver.** ## Long-Term Collaboration This is an ongoing project, not a one-time assignment. The websites involved may change regularly. Therefore, I need someone available for continued development, debugging, updates, optimization, and maintenance. ## Mandatory Language Requirement **You MUST understand and communicate effectively in Bangla (বাংলা).** All project requirements, technical discussions, troubleshooting, and ongoing communication may be conducted in Bangla. Please do not apply if you cannot communicate in Bangla. ## How to Apply Please include: 1. A brief introduction and your technical background 2. Examples of relevant browser automation, website analysis, or reverse engineering projects 3. Your experience with JavaScript, Python, Tampermonkey, and browser debugging 4. Your approach to investigating complex website behavior and technical problems 5. Your availability for long-term collaboration 6. Your estimated timeline and hourly or project-based rate Shortlisted candidates may be offered a small paid technical assessment based on a real project requirement. ## Final Note **I'm hiring a problem-solver, not just a programmer.** If you can independently investigate complex website behavior, understand browser and network operations, identify technical problems, and deliver reliable end-to-end solutions, I'd like to hear from you. **Only experienced developers with relevant expertise and Bangla communication skills should apply.**

gig.title: Android Cloud Postgres Data Viewer
gig.description: I’m putting together an Android Studio app whose only job is to pull product records from a Postgres instance hosted on Google Cloud and show them in a clean, scrollable list. The data connection must run through Google’s Antigravity agent so the app stays lightweight and secure without shipping database credentials inside the APK. Here’s what I need from you: • A minimal yet solid Android Studio project (Kotlin or Java—your choice) that connects to the Postgres database via the Antigravity agent. • An async call that fetches product data—name, price, description, image URL are enough for a working demo—and maps it into a RecyclerView list. • Basic UI: toolbar with app name, RecyclerView list, placeholder images handled gracefully, and swipe-to-refresh. Material 3 components are preferred. • Clear, commented code showing how the Antigravity client is initialised, how credentials/tokens are kept out of the app, and how the query is structured. • A short README explaining local setup, required Google Cloud roles/APIs, and how to point the build at a different Cloud SQL instance. Acceptance criteria 1. Clean build in the latest stable Android Studio without manual tweaks. 2. On launch, the list populates from our Cloud SQL Postgres via Antigravity; offline or auth errors are surfaced with a Snackbar. 3. No hard-coded keys or passwords inside the repo; connection details are read from secure config or runtime. If you have previous experience with Google Cloud SQL, Cloud Build, or similar connector agents, that’s a big plus—I’m aiming to keep the cloud side as managed as possible. Let me know how quickly you can spin up a proof of concept and what you’ll need from my end (service account, sample schema, etc.).

gig.title: Tracking & Measurement Specialist Required
gig.description: Tracking & Measurement Specialist (Server-side GTM / Stape / Meta CAPI) – Contract About us Java Whiskers runs cat cafés in London (White City and Marylebone) and Sweden. Tickets are sold through Roller, which is embedded in an iframe on our site. We advertise on Meta, TikTok and Google Ads, and work with Awin affiliates. The situation In September we launched a new UK website with a new tracking setup: a GTM web container, a server-side GTM container on Stape, Meta CAPI, TikTok Events API, GA4 and Awin. Since the launch our UK sales have dropped from +6–16% year over year to −7–14%, and our ad platforms are receiving poor-quality signals. We’ve already completed an internal audit, documented every issue and fixed the most urgent ones. We now need an experienced specialist to finish the job, verify everything end to end and make sure our data can be trusted. What’s already been found and partly fixed Meta received placeholder or invalid email addresses (over 50% of server events) and mismatched purchase value/currency (88% of purchases). Hashing, validation and value mapping were fixed on 6 October and need verifying. The share of purchases tracked by the browser pixel versus the server dropped to about 30%, because the pixel didn’t fire after cookie consent. This is partly fixed for Meta, but not yet for TikTok. Event IDs for deduplication were unstable. This is fixed and needs verifying. What we need you to do Verify and complete Verify the changes already made, using GTM preview (web and server), Meta Test Events and TikTok Events Manager. Finish the remaining fixes: TikTok pixel firing after consent Duplicate page_view events from SPA history changes (GA4 shows around 15 page views per session) Correct order value sent to Awin Splitting add_to_cart from begin_checkout, which currently fire on the same Roller step A domain allowlist in Meta Events Manager Bring Meta Event Match Quality above 7 for purchases. Fix attribution Around 50% of GA4 revenue is “Unassigned” or “Direct”. The Roller checkout iframe grants consent automatically and starts new sessions.
